'''Shark fin soup''', or '''shark fin stew''', is a [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] believed to have originated from China. On the Chinese seas during the 1800s, pirates under the control of Ch'ing Yih Szaou used to make shark fin soup that took at least 4 hours to prepare.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Klausmann |first1=Ulrike |last2=Meinzerin |first2=Marion |last3=Kuhn |first3=Gabriel |authorlink3=Gabriel_Kuhn |title=Women Pirates and the Politics of the Jolly Roger |edition=1st |year=1997 |publisher=Black Rose Books Ltd |location=C.P. 1258 Succ. Place du Parc Montreal, Quebec, Canada H2W2R3 |language=English |isbn=1-55164-058-9 |page=192}}</ref>

Recipes for shark fin soup vary, but shark fin is an essential ingredient. In recent years, it has been criticized for its negative impact on shark populations.

==Ingredients==
===Soup===
*400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] shark fins
*100 g dried, ground [[Cookbook:Shrimp|shrimp]]
*10 large dried Dongu mushrooms
*50 g dried [[Cookbook:Bamboo Shoot|bamboo shoots]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] root
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|fat]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
*4 tbsp Chinese white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
*¾ [[Cookbook:Liter|liter]] chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
*Fish [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]] from red-boiled fins
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]

==Procedure== 
#Clean the fins and place in lukewarm water.
#Soak ground shrimp and dried mushrooms for 30 minutes in ¼ litre warm water. The water can then be discarded. The dried bamboo should also be soaked until soft, then cut into thin strips.
#Thoroughly clean and scale the shark fins, then place in a litre of water. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for 1 hour. Afterwards, set the water aside.
#Place fins in a fresh litre of water and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 1½ hours. Afterwards, strain fins.
#In a separate pot, add chicken broth and bring to a boil. Add ginger and shrimp and simmer for 30 minutes.
#Remove from heat and strain the broth, discarding the shrimp and ginger. 
#In a separate pot, heat the bacon fat, adding the bamboo shoots and mushrooms together with salt.
#[[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] for 1 minute, then add soy sauce, wine, broth, fish stock, and fins. Boil over low heat, stirring frequently, for 20 minutes.
#Remove from heat and slowly stir in the corn starch, in small increments. Sprinkle sesame oil on the soup.
#Serve in a large bowl. The shark fins should remain on the surface.

steps.text: Clean the fins and place in lukewarm water.
Soak ground shrimp and dried mushrooms for 30 minutes in ¼ litre warm water. The water can then be discarded. The dried bamboo should also be soaked until soft, then cut into thin strips.
Thoroughly clean and scale the shark fins, then place in a litre of water. Simmer for 1 hour. Afterwards, set the water aside.
Place fins in a fresh litre of water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 1½ hours. Afterwards, strain fins.
In a separate pot, add chicken broth and bring to a boil. Add ginger and shrimp and simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove from heat and strain the broth, discarding the shrimp and ginger.
In a separate pot, heat the bacon fat, adding the bamboo shoots and mushrooms together with salt.
Sauté for 1 minute, then add soy sauce, wine, broth, fish stock, and fins. Boil over low heat, stirring frequently, for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and slowly stir in the corn starch, in small increments. Sprinkle sesame oil on the soup.
Serve in a large bowl. The shark fins should remain on the surface.
